phase: Existing claims and settlement processing; new administrative claims closed
phaseDetail: DOJ reports more than $1 billion in settlement offers and more than $827 million paid as of August 10, 2026. The Navy no longer accepts new CLJA administrative claims after August 10, 2024. Timely claims still require attention to documents, denial notices, individual litigation deadlines and settlement terms.
defendants: United States of America (Department of the Navy)

settlements.label: Elective Option and CLJA settlement activity
settlements.amount: More than $1 billion offered; more than $827 million paid (August 10, 2026)
settlements.detail: DOJ’s August 10, 2026 totals describe aggregate CLJA settlement activity. EO diagnosis and exposure tiers range from $100,000 to $450,000, with a further $100,000 for qualifying deaths. Individual eligibility and payment depend on the applicable program and completed documents; aggregate totals are not average awards.
settlements.individualClaims: DOJ says accepted EO offers can be paid within 60 days or less with timely, accurate payment documents. That is not a deadline for receiving an offer.

deadlineOverride: The Navy stopped accepting new Camp Lejeune Justice Act administrative claims after August 10, 2024. State personal-injury deadlines do not reopen that federal window. A timely administrative claim does not eliminate later deadlines following denial, court orders or settlement offers; the notice and individual claim history need separate review.

updateNote: Earlier court and administrative claim totals were removed because the cited pages did not substantiate those dated figures. Filed administrative claims and filed lawsuits are different measures and are not interchangeable with pending cases.

updates.summary: DOJ reports more than $1 billion in settlement offers and more than $827 million paid across CLJA settlements.
The Navy continues reviewing existing claims and requesting supporting records; new administrative claims remain closed.
The Navy portal supports claim-status checks, document uploads and claim-specific messages for existing claims.
DOJ distinguishes accepted EO payment processing from the uncertain timing of an initial offer.
